signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: CHF 1W avg +0.844% across n=6 pairs versus JPY −0.723% across n=7 pairs establishes a G10 spread of 1.567%, clearing the critical threshold. SNB SARON at −0.04% versus TONA at 0.98% leaves CHF carrying a 102bp rate deficit relative to JPY that the safe-haven bid entirely overrides in the current cross-asset environment. The SNB 0.0% policy rate against BoJ at 1.25% yields a −125bp nominal carry differential that fails to dent the leading G10 currency's momentum. Trade bias: Long CHF/JPY; safe-haven demand dominates carry differentials. Catalyst: SNB interest rate decision and monetary policy assessment. Risk: Risk-on sentiment returns with VIX breaking below 14, removing the safe-haven premium and exposing the underlying carry disadvantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.92, holding above the SMA20 at 156.61 while capped by the SMA50 at 158.85. SOFR at 3.85% versus TONA at 0.98% maintains a 287bp OIS carry premium supporting the long-USD carry trade. Options pricing shows a 25d RR at −2.27, reflecting strong put skew as the options market heavily bids downside protection against intervention. CFTC leveraged funds hold a net long position of +20,069 contracts, corresponding to the 95th percentile of the trailing 52-week range with a z-score of +1.57, marking extreme positioning on the long side. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported with elevated options hedging against verbal warnings. Catalyst: BoJ trimmed mean core CPI and weighted median core CPI releases. Risk: Sustained break above 158.85 triggers accelerated option-delta buying and forces short-covering.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Vol + Technicals
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1413, positioned below the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1576/1.1542/1.1629. SOFR at 3.85% versus €STR at 2.44% provides a 141bp OIS carry differential favoring the dollar. Implied volatility sits at 4.9% against an HV30 of 4.4%, producing a positive volatility risk premium of +0.5% while the 25d RR at −0.33 indicates mild put skew. CFTC leveraged funds maintain a net short position of −51,355 contracts at the 32nd percentile of its 52-week range, accompanied by retail sentiment showing 71% long and 29% short. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by hawkish Federal Reserve rate expectations and steady dollar resilience. Catalyst: ECB executive board member Schnabel speech and economic bulletin. Risk: Break above the SMA20 at 1.1576 invalidates the technical downside structure and forces short covering.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Central Bank Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3279, remaining below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3491/1.3482/1.3454. SOFR at 3.85% versus SONIA at 3.73% maintains a modest 12bp OIS carry advantage for the dollar. CFTC leveraged funds hold a net long position of +18,698 contracts at the 60th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of +0.28, while retail sentiment shows 69% long. The 25d risk reversal prints at −0.49, reflecting mild put skew as options markets hedge against further downside. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, pressured by central bank policy divergence and declining short-term rate expectations. Catalyst: BoE MPC member Dhingra speech. Risk: Sustained break back above the SMA200 at 1.3454 invalidates the bearish continuation setup.
